A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TACO and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The renamed method and reorganized appendices can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original TACO benchmark results, component ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative segmentation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and qualitative results and adds S4 sensitivity experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The renamed Sem co-NMF retains the semantic anchors, minimum cross-entropy alignment penalty, temporal regularization, and FC-CLIP prompting already present in v1. Removing reconstruction weights from the equations matches their previously specified unit values. The KL alternative is an ablation, not a replacement of the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same binary and semantic segmentation coverage: S4, MS3, ADE Sound Prompted, AVSS, and ADE Sound Prompted Semantic. The new sensitivity experiments use the existing S4 dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds TACO without the segmenter to the main AVS-Bench comparison; this variant already appeared in other comparisons in v1. External comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding AVS-Bench and ADE Sound Prompted tables.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces controlled S4 experiments varying K across 6, 8, 10, and 12, beta_p across 100, 125, and 150, and randomly retaining half or one-quarter of the word bank. The retained benchmark protocols, backbones, metrics, 1800 optimization steps, and learning rate remain unchanged as documented.

E4.justification: Appendix B substantially expands sensitivity analysis by testing factor count, penalty strength, cross-entropy versus KL divergence, and word-bank size. Earlier component ablations, clamping, runtime, semantic limitations, and failure analyses remain. One of the seven MS3 qualitative examples in v1 Figure 9 is omitted from v2 Figure 10.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions and retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting in the main result tables. However, the new NMF sensitivity Tables 6–7 provide only point estimates, making uncertainty reporting less complete for the added analyses. No increase or decrease in run counts is documented.

E6.justification: MS3 TACO mask-IoU/F-score changes from 50.46/58.11 in v1 Table 2 to 43.15/47.50 in v2 Table 1, while ACL-SSL remains at 41.08/46.67. The MS3 word-bank ranking reverses: general 50.45 versus specific 47.23 becomes general 43.15 versus specific 45.15. v2 also adds sensitivity and AVS-Bench ablation results. Its unrefined S4 scores differ between Tables 1 and 3 without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: The factorization definitions, semantic descriptors, alignment objective, and temporal regularizer retain the same mathematical substance. Unit-weight simplification and temporal-weight renaming do not introduce new theory. Algorithm 1 presents existing computations rather than a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a training-free, interpretable approach using frozen representations and state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation performance. The additional Sem co-NMF contribution bullet highlights semantic alignment already described and claimed in v1 rather than establishing a new contribution.

C2.justification: v1 explains the general word bank's MS3 advantage through broader concepts covering multiple sources; v2 removes that explanation and describes a specific-bank advantage. v2 also interprets the new sensitivity results and corrects the stated direction of the unrefined ADE word-bank effect. Existing semantic-class assignment and CLAP-related failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses Gaussian matrix initialization and adds static-frame pseudocode with instructions to include temporal regularization for video. The code-release promise becomes explicitly open-source upon acceptance. Existing backbone, hardware, and default optimization information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds supervised segmentation references by Gao et al. and Liu et al. and more explicitly distinguishes supervised from unsupervised approaches. It also changes the description of ADE comparators from task-specific fine-tuning to training on audio-image pairs. The central positioning relative to NMF and prior unsupervised methods remains.

P1.justification: The title and method terminology change, with localized rewrites of the contributions, motivation, method explanation, and qualitative discussion. Citation style changes, the clamping analysis moves to the appendix, and lettered appendices and an Impact Statement are introduced. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the appendices into full-width pages and enlarges and relocates qualitative figures. It adds two sensitivity tables, Algorithm 1, and a decomposition diagram, modifies Figure 1 to show the word bank, and adds a segmenter column to the main AVS-Bench table. The MS3 qualitative grid loses one row.

improvement.justification: Appendix B provides useful sensitivity evidence for choices largely fixed without such analysis in v1, while the decomposition diagram and explicit segmenter labels improve transparency. These are limited gains over v1's already extensive evaluation. They are tempered by missing uncertainty in the new tables, pseudocode that omits explicit constraint enforcement, and unresolved result-reporting inconsistencies. The lower MS3 scores alone do not establish deterioration.
